title: No orchestration retry loop exists: failed runs leave signals orphaned at spec_written with no automated re-entry path
description: The canonical pipeline is: signal_fix → spec (status: spec_written) → run → candidate (status: candidate). When run fails the QA gate, the signal is left at spec_written with no automated mechanism to retry. There is no orchestrator that: (a) detects the run failed, (b) determines whether a re-fix is warranted vs. a rubric adjustment, (c) triggers a new signal_fix → spec → run cycle on the same signal. Orphaned spec_written signals accumulate silently. The only recovery path is manual human intervention.
proposed_resolution:
Design and implement an orchestration role (building on run-auditor from a1000052) that monitors run completion events and handles the retry decision:
1. On run QA gate failure: inspect qa_gate_failures (from a1000058); if root cause is a code defect, re-enter signal_fix with the failed run's diagnostic context as additional input; if root cause is a rubric configuration issue, surface to human for rubric review.
2. On run success: advance signal status (per a1000059).
3. Add a 'retry_count' field to run artifacts to bound infinite retry loops.
4. Define a maximum retry threshold (e.g. 3) after which the signal escalates to redesign (per a1000009).
